style: An oil painting of 1893, painted alla prima in the manner of Sargent, Atkinson Grimshaw and the Victorian narrative painters: visible loose brushstrokes, thick impasto in the lights, thin transparent glazes in the shadows, soft lost edges, broken colour, canvas weave showing through; night, deep shadows, warm lamplight against cold blue darkness, in the dark tone of a gothic Victorian nocturne; figures small or in silhouette, no detailed faces. Not an illustration, not digital art. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, lettering, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Shot: far, exterior, looking in. Seen from the dark garden of the asylum through a tall lit window: inside, a study with a fire, a group of men in chairs and a young woman listening to a man reading from pages; cold blue night outside, ivy on the brick.

Shot: very wide interior from the far dark corner of a book-lined study at night: firelight, a group of figures gathered round the fire seen from behind, lamplight on papers, the rest of the room in deep shadow.
Shot: wide, interior. A long asylum corridor at night lit by one oil lamp; an attendant sits on a wooden chair outside a closed cell door, listening, his shadow long on the wall.
Shot: establishing, far. The asylum at Purfleet at night under a windy moonlit sky, bare trees thrashing, one upper window lit; the lawn and a stone statue in the foreground in cold blue light.
Shot: medium-wide, no people. A heavy cell door in an asylum corridor at night, a lamp on the floor, the observation trap open and a thin line of light beneath the door, deep shadows.
Shot: establishing, far. The asylum at Purfleet at nightfall, the study windows glowing warm on the ground floor, a carriage drawn up on the gravel, deep blue sky with the last light.
